LESSON: WRITING 1.5.1 WRITING LEGIBLY AND NEATLY

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.5: Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly, part of Strand 1 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should one write legibly and neatly? 2. What are the qualities of a good handwriting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. copy a provided passage and shape upper and lower case lettters appropriately,

2. copy a provided passage and space letters, words and sentences correctly,

3. rewrite a provided text legibly and neatly,

4. cancel words or sentences neatly

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. copy a provided passage and shape upper and lower case lettters appropriately,
2. copy a provided passage and space letters, words and sentences correctly,
3. rewrite a provided text legibly and neatly,
4. cancel words or sentences neatly

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 1.5.1 Writing legibly and neatly together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner completes tasks on time as he or she writes texts legibly and neatly.

• Self-efficacy: It is enhanced as the learner’s confidence in written communication is boosted.

Values:
Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner legibly and neatly writes words and sentences related to human rights.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Effective communication: It is improved as the learner practises writing legibly and neatly.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to apply the skill of writing neatly and legibly while writing essays in Religious Education.
